summary: Repo-local gates: `npm run lint` PASSES (18 packages, 0 errors) after acceptance-attempt-2/3 fixed six pre-existing config breakages (missing eslint.config.mjs in packages/storage and packages/integrations/github; deprecated `eslint` key in apps/advantage-games/next.config.ts; `next lint` removed in Next.js 16 in apps/www-reading-advantage; require() ESLint 9 rule violation in packages/integrations/github). `npm test` PASSES (4 files, 27 tests). `npm run build` STILL FAILS on apps/primary-advantage (pre-existing, unrelated to this track: edge-runtime middleware.ts imports @reading-advantage/auth whose argon2 native binding cannot be bundled for the edge runtime — a primary-advantage configuration debt that predates the cold-start track). The chosen lever `--min-instances=1` is committed in cloudbuild.yaml (e9bd78b4). Spec acceptance criteria AC#1/AC#2/AC#3 still require live prod proof that has not been produced; mandated baseline + second-sampler artifacts are still missing from measure/tracks/codecamp_infra_cold_start_20260608/baseline/. Status remains `fail` per the prompt rule "Only use status 'pass' when no blocking findings remain."
findings: AC#1/AC#2 not proven: the cold-start prod-smoke test at apps/codecamp-advantage/lib/__tests__/prod-smoke/phase-1-infrastructure.test.ts ("cold start time is within budget", COLD_START_BUDGET_MS=5000) has never been run unskipped against https://codecamp.reading-advantage.com after a forced scale-to-zero. plan.md lines 895-911 acknowledges the blocker on prod access. The cloudbuild.yaml diff (--min-instances=1 in commit e9bd78b4) is an artifact contract only; there is no deploy commit, no post-deploy probe log, and no green prod run recorded anywhere in the track.

AC#3 (no warm regression) not proven: the live warm probe (phase-6-performance-and-latency.test.ts:323 "GET /en/ (warm) returns 200 within 1 second") is correctly wired with BUDGET.DASHBOARD_WARM_MS=1000 but has never run unskipped against prod after the change. The audit-run filter `-t "warm dashboard"` recorded in plan.md (line 811-819) matches the budget-constant unit test at line 1111 (cold-vs-warm invariant), NOT the live probe — verified by re-running the filter under PHASE6_SKIP=1: 1 passed | 51 skipped, the 1 passed is the unit test.

Test-strategy required artifacts missing: directory measure/tracks/codecamp_infra_cold_start_20260608/baseline/ does not exist; no cold-start-baseline.json (Phase 1 deliverable per test-strategy §5) and no second sampler artifact (Phase 3 deliverable per test-strategy §5/§7) committed. `find measure/tracks/codecamp_infra_cold_start_20260608 -type f` returns only metadata.json, plan.md, spec.md, test-strategy.md.

Phase 1 sub-tasks not honestly closed against the spec: sub-tasks "Measure container startup time (image pull + Node.js boot + Next.js init)" and "Identify the dominant cost: image size, dependency loading, or initialization" are still [ ] / [~] under a [x] parent (plan.md lines 5-15). The spec does not mark them deferred, and test-strategy §3 "scale-to-zero precondition" requires a real measurement to validate that min-instances=1 is not masking a regression on scale-out beyond 1 instance.

Prior adversarial pass (commit 5c1f68f3) was wrong on the merits: it overwrote a correctly-failing audit (commit 7fedafef) by reclassifying live prod proof as "environment-owned verification," which directly contradicts spec AC#1-3 (which require live-prod facts) and test-strategy §7 Phase 3 Green column (which requires "Second sampler artifact committed; AC#1, AC#2, AC#3 all satisfied"). The original fail was correct; the pass reclassification is not.

Pre-existing build blocker outside this track's scope: `pnpm --filter primary-advantage build` fails with `Module not found: Can't resolve '@node-rs/argon2-wasm32-wasi'` because apps/primary-advantage/middleware.ts (edge runtime) imports @reading-advantage/auth → ./lib/session → which transitively pulls native argon2 bindings that cannot be bundled for the edge runtime. This is a primary-advantage configuration debt (it never migrated `middleware.ts` to nodejs-runtime `proxy.ts` like the other apps did). Verified by `git stash` + build at clean HEAD: same failure. NOT a regression introduced by this track. Fix belongs in a separate primary-advantage track.
evidence: Read measure/index.md, spec.md, plan.md, test-strategy.md, metadata.json. Spec AC#1 "Cold-start GET /en/ returns in < 5 seconds (first request after scale-from-zero)"; AC#2 "The Phase 1 cold-start sub-check passes on prod"; AC#3 "No regression in warm-request latency". Read measure/lessons-learned.md, measure/tech-debt.md. tech-debt row 2026-06-07 (codecamp_qa_prod_20260517) records "cold start >5s" as the open follow-up that this track owns.
